primitives.name: AnthropicProvider
primitives.when: you want Claude models as the Loop's provider — native Messages API with opt-in prompt caching and thinking-block passthrough
primitives.fails: throws on a missing apiKey; normalizes stopReason and usage (usage:null when the API omits it); a socket idle/deadline/transport cut rejects with a retryable Timeout/ProviderError.
primitives.example: const provider = new AnthropicProvider({ apiKey, model: 'claude-sonnet-5' });

primitives.name: assessComplexity
primitives.when: you want a fast, no-LLM read of how hard a goal is (simple/medium/complex/critical) to decide whether to invoke the Planner
primitives.fails: never throws — pure text scoring; non-string/blank input scores lowest. Keyword lists are frozen and a critical-safety override always wins.
primitives.example:
const { level, needsPlanning } = assessComplexity(goal);
if (needsPlanning) await planner.plan(goal);

primitives.name: buildExactTool
primitives.when: you want an embeddings-free, exact AND-term filter handle over a slice-source — complete over its slices, for precise lexical matches
primitives.fails: only as good as a lexical rule; complete over the slices it is given (no recall cap) but matches nothing outside them.
primitives.example:
const tool = buildExactTool(corpus);
await recurse(task, ctx, { retrieval: 'exact', tools: [tool] });

primitives.name: buildMetaTools
primitives.when: you want the two bulk MCP meta-tools (mcp_discover, mcp_invoke) instead of exposing every discovered tool individually — one gate-check per invocation
primitives.fails: returns [mcp_discover, mcp_invoke]; a tool name does not travel as action.type (a deliberate v0.9 trade for one gate-check per call).
primitives.example: const metaTools = buildMetaTools(tools);

primitives.name: buildScanTool
primitives.when: you need the complete count/"all" path — scan every slice + LLM-judge + code-count — the only retrieval mode that can honestly answer "how many"
primitives.signature: buildScanTool(corpus: Slice[] | (() => Promise<Slice[]>), opts: {provider: Provider, window?: number, passes?: number, ctx?: object, onLlmResult?: Function, policy?: Function}) => ToolDef
primitives.fails: a dead window surfaces as `INCOMPLETE — the count is a floor`, never a clean number over a hole; a governance HaltError propagates clean.
primitives.example:
const tool = buildScanTool(corpus, { provider, window: 8 });
await recurse('how many mention X', ctx, { tools: [tool] });

primitives.name: buildSearchTool
primitives.when: you want to give a recurse worker a needle-search handle over litectx (embeddings recall for the relevant few) — for FINDING, never counting
primitives.signature: buildSearchTool(litectx: {recall: Function}, opts?: {kinds?: string[], n?: number}) => ToolDef
primitives.fails: returns matched bodies only and CANNOT count (the completeness guard blocks a "how many" ask before it is offered); a dead window yields nothing, never a fabricated hit.
primitives.example:
const tool = buildSearchTool(litectx, { n: 8 });
await recurse(task, ctx, { retrieval: 'search', tools: [tool] });

primitives.name: calibrate
primitives.when: you are admitting an LLM tier to the judge role and need to grade it against the frozen clear-case battery and resist every injection style before trusting it
primitives.signature: calibrate(opts: object) => Promise<ReturnType<typeof gradeRun> & { reps:number, floor:number, totalCostUsd:number|null, unpricedCalls:number, injectionBattery: { styles: Array<{label:string, usable:number, broke:number, resisted:boolean}>, allResisted:boolean, leaks:number } }>
primitives.fails: never fabricates a pass — a leak in any injection style blocks admission even above the clear-case floor, and the negative control must fail the set. HaltError propagates clean.
primitives.example:
const report = await calibrate({ provider, reps: 5, floor: 7 });
if (!report.injectionBattery.allResisted) reject('injection leak');

primitives.name: calibrateJev
primitives.when: you are admitting a Jev model tier to the classify role and must grade it against the frozen clear-case battery AND prove it resists every injection style before trusting it on untrusted input
primitives.signature: calibrateJev(opts: object) => Promise<{reps:number, floor:number, clear: ReturnType<typeof gradeJevRun>, injection: {styles: Array<{label:string, style:string, usable:number, resisted:boolean}>, allResisted:boolean, leaks:number}, admitted:boolean}>
primitives.fails: never fabricates a pass — a leak in any injection style blocks admission even above the clear-case floor, and the negative control must fail the set; a governance HaltError propagates clean.

primitives.name: Checkpoint
primitives.when: you want an always-prompt human-in-the-loop approval gate on chosen tools — complementary to bareguard's policy-driven pauses
primitives.fails: auto-denies on timeout (0 disables) and denies safe when no reply channel is wired; a TimeoutError is surfaced, never swallowed.
primitives.example:
const checkpoint = new Checkpoint({ tools: ['deploy'], waitForReply });
const ok = await checkpoint.confirm('deploy', args);

primitives.name: CircuitBreaker
primitives.when: you want per-key failure isolation — trip open after N failures, probe half-open after a cooldown — so one failing dependency doesn't cascade
primitives.fails: throws CircuitOpenError while open (fail-fast, no downstream call); transitions emit onStateChange and reset on a successful half-open probe.
primitives.example:
const cb = new CircuitBreaker({ threshold: 5 });
await cb.call('api', () => fetch(url));

primitives.name: CLIPipeProvider
primitives.when: you want to drive a CLI (e.g. the claude CLI) as the Loop's provider — native MCP tools or a JSON emulation envelope
primitives.fails: throws on a missing command; in native mode it owns its own cycle (ownsCycle), so per-round Loop seams are refused at construction rather than left silently dead.
primitives.example: const provider = new CLIPipeProvider({ command: 'claude' });

primitives.name: createBrowsingTools
primitives.when: you want to give an agent browser tools (navigate, click, read) via barebrowse for inline snapshots
primitives.signature: createBrowsingTools(opts?: object) => Promise<{tools: Array, close: Function}|null>
primitives.fails: returns null if barebrowse (optional dep) is not installed; otherwise returns {tools, close} — call close() to release the browser.
primitives.example:
const b = await createBrowsingTools();
const loop = new Loop({ provider, tools: b.tools });

primitives.name: createDeferTool
primitives.when: you want a tool that queues an action to a JSONL file for an external waker (cron) to fire later — two-phase governance (emit-time + fire-time)
primitives.signature: createDeferTool(options?: object) => {tool: ToolDef, readQueue: () => Promise<Record<string, any>[]>, queuePath: string}
primitives.fails: returns {tool, readQueue, queuePath}; the inner action is re-gated at fire time when the waker runs. bareguard caps via defer.ratePerMinute.
primitives.example:
const { tool } = createDeferTool();
const loop = new Loop({ provider, tools: [tool] });

primitives.name: createMCPBridge
primitives.when: you want to auto-discover MCP servers and expose them as bareagent tools in one call — with a trust hook gating command execution
primitives.signature: createMCPBridge(opts?: object) => Promise<{tools: ToolDef[], metaTools?: ToolDef[], servers: string[], systemContext: string, denied: DeniedTool[], errors?: Array<{server: string, error: string}>, close: Function}>
primitives.fails: a trust hook returning false skips a server (its command never runs) and a throw is fail-closed (deny); returns tools plus a close() to shut servers down.
primitives.example:
const { tools, close } = await createMCPBridge();
const loop = new Loop({ provider, tools });

primitives.name: createMobileTools
primitives.when: you want to give an agent Android/iOS device control (tap, type, snapshot) via baremobile
primitives.signature: createMobileTools(opts?: object) => Promise<{tools: ToolDef[], close: Function}|null>
primitives.fails: returns null if baremobile (optional dep) is not installed; otherwise returns {tools, close} — call close() to disconnect.
primitives.example:
const m = await createMobileTools({ platform: 'android' });
const loop = new Loop({ provider, tools: m.tools });

primitives.name: createShellTools
primitives.when: you want to give an agent shell/file tools (read, grep, write, edit, run, exec) — cross-platform, pure Node, zero deps
primitives.fails: never throws at creation; gating is the caller's via Loop({ policy }) and fs.writeScope, and shell_edit refuses a non-unique anchor as a tool result (file untouched).
primitives.example:
const { tools } = createShellTools();
const loop = new Loop({ provider, tools, policy });

primitives.name: createSpawnTool
primitives.when: you want an LLM-callable spawn tool so a model can fork child bareagents itself — governed per-family by bareguard
primitives.signature: createSpawnTool(options?: object) => {tool: ToolDef, spawnChild: typeof spawnChild}
primitives.fails: returns {tool, spawnChild}; the tool blocks per child and child stderr is re-emitted as child:stderr on the wired Stream.
primitives.example:
const { tool } = createSpawnTool();
const loop = new Loop({ provider, tools: [tool] });

primitives.name: createStashSkill
primitives.when: you need compaction-first context hygiene — a registrable skill whose checkpoint/compact/restore tools fold the live transcript at round boundaries
primitives.signature: createStashSkill(options?: Object) => { skill: { name: string, description: string, instructions: string, tools: ToolDef[] }, trim: (msgs: any[], ctx: any) => Promise<any[]>, restoreHandles: () => string[] }
primitives.fails: never throws for a fold; degrades LOUDLY to a lossless park when summarize is unwired. Preserves tool-pairing and role alternation by construction.
primitives.example:
const { skill, trim } = createStashSkill({ compaction: { ceilingTokens: 100000 } });
const loop = new Loop({ provider, trim });

primitives.name: discoverServers
primitives.when: you want to find configured MCP servers from the trusted $HOME/IDE config paths (or explicit paths) — discovery without invoking them
primitives.signature: discoverServers(configPaths?: string[], opts?: { includeProjectConfig?: boolean }) => Map<string, ServerDef>
primitives.fails: honors explicit configPaths verbatim and scans trusted defaults otherwise; returns a Map and never executes a server command.
primitives.example: const servers = discoverServers();

primitives.name: Evaluator
primitives.when: you need to judge an output against a goal or contract — deterministically (predicate), by LLM rubric, or with a tool-running critic that exercises the live artifact
primitives.fails: never throws for a bad grade — returns a Verdict {status: satisfied|needs_revision|failed}; a provider HaltError propagates clean. Judge tokens forward via onLlmResult.

primitives.name: FallbackProvider
primitives.when: you want to try several providers in order, failing over to the next when one errors — resilience across tiers or vendors
primitives.fails: throws if given no providers; returns the first provider's success, else propagates the last provider's error.
primitives.example: const provider = new FallbackProvider([primary, backup]);

primitives.name: GeminiProvider
primitives.when: you want Gemini models as the Loop's provider — native generateContent with implicit prompt caching
primitives.fails: throws on a missing apiKey; normalizes stopReason (promoting a complete tool call) and usage; a socket idle/deadline/transport cut rejects with a retryable error.
primitives.example: const provider = new GeminiProvider({ apiKey, model: 'gemini-2.5-pro' });

primitives.name: harvestKey
primitives.when: you need the stable content-address for a transcript unit (the key harvest-before-evict writes under) — a collision-resistant 64-bit id
primitives.fails: never throws; normal provider ids round-trip unchanged, and two near-independent hash streams avoid 32-bit birthday collisions.
primitives.example: const key = harvestKey(unit); // stable id for this turn's harvest

primitives.name: isCritical
primitives.when: you want the durable critical-safety floor alone (security/production/compliance/financial) to gate extra scrutiny, without the full scorer
primitives.fails: never throws — deterministic override; non-string/blank input is false. This floor is non-overridable by design.
primitives.example: if (isCritical(goal)) verdict = await evaluator.evaluate(goal, result, { contract });

primitives.name: JevProvider
primitives.when: you need a cheap, fast, calibrated classifier (yes/no, pick-one, or a score) instead of a full LLM grading round — the cost tier below judge/Evaluator.rubric
primitives.fails: classify() throws ValidationError (stamped lib:'bare-agent') on a bad request or a malformed/mismatched Jev reply; ProviderError on HTTP/transport (401/403/422/429/529, socket cut); a governance HaltError from onLlmResult propagates clean.

primitives.name: JsonFile
primitives.when: you want zero-dependency JSON-file storage for Memory (store/search/get/delete) — the simplest durable backend, no native deps
primitives.fails: throws on a missing path; implements the four-verb Store socket over a plain JSON file.
primitives.example: const store = new JsonFile({ path: './agent.json' });

primitives.name: JsonlTransport
primitives.when: you want to pipe structured Stream events as JSONL to a writable stream — pipe-friendly observability
primitives.fails: never throws on write; defaults to process.stdout when no output stream is given.
primitives.example: const stream = new Stream({ transport: new JsonlTransport() });

primitives.name: judge
primitives.when: you need a decisive honored/broke verdict on whether one egress artifact honored the verbatim request — a return-time integrity check
primitives.fails: throws ValidationError on bad inputs; HaltError propagates clean. Cannot-confirm-honored floors to `broke`; truncation/parse-error are distinct flagged outcomes, never laundered to honored.
primitives.example:
const { verdict, where } = await judge({ request, artifact, provider });
if (verdict === 'broke') flag(where);

primitives.name: judgeToAnnotation
primitives.when: you want to surface a judge() verdict on a gate's audit/humanChannel via gate.annotate, keeping the render pure (it never calls the gate)
primitives.signature: judgeToAnnotation(verdict: JudgeVerdict | { verdict?: string, where?: any }, opts?: JudgeToAnnotationOptions) => Annotation
primitives.fails: never throws and never calls the gate; surfaces fail-open (a non-honored verdict surfaces) and bounds fields against the sink's silent caps with a visible clip marker.
primitives.example: gate.annotate(judgeToAnnotation(await judge({ request, artifact, provider })));

primitives.name: litectxCorpus
primitives.when: you want a resident slice-source that paginates a litectx corpus via enumerate — for a corpus ALREADY in litectx, feeding scan/partition
primitives.signature: litectxCorpus(litectx: {enumerate: Function}, opts?: {kind?: 'fact'|'episode', pageSize?: number}) => () => Promise<Slice[]>
primitives.fails: never ingests a fresh corpus (strictly worse than scanning an in-hand array); returns an async source materialized once and cached.
primitives.example:
const corpus = litectxCorpus(litectx, { kind: 'fact' });
await recurse(task, ctx, { mode: 'partition', corpus });

primitives.name: liteCtxMcpBridgeConfig
primitives.when: you want to connect a litectx instance to a bareagent runner over the MCP bridge — a curated, child-db-local litectx server
primitives.fails: read-only by default (opt-in `writable` allows remember/forget); pre-seeding `now` makes createMCPBridge skip IDE discovery and connect straight to this server.
primitives.example:
const cfg = liteCtxMcpBridgeConfig({ root: './child.db' });
const { tools } = await createMCPBridge({ config: cfg });

primitives.name: Loop
primitives.when: you are running a model think/act/observe cycle and need round accounting, tool dispatch, spin guards, and a governance chokepoint
primitives.fails: returns the last assistant text with an `error` tag on any bound (halt/deny-streak/truncation/provider error); throws only if constructed without a provider. A policy HaltError exits clean.

primitives.name: Memory
primitives.when: you want thin store-backed memory (store/search/get/delete) an agent can write to and recall from, over any swappable backend
primitives.fails: throws if constructed without a store; recall/store metering is opt-in via ctx. All persistence delegates to the backend.
primitives.example:
const memory = new Memory({ store: new JsonFile({ path: './mem.json' }) });
await memory.store({ text: 'a durable fact' });

primitives.name: OllamaProvider
primitives.when: you want local models via Ollama as the Loop's provider — no API key, self-hosted
primitives.fails: normalizes stopReason (promoting a complete tool call) and usage; a malformed tool-call JSON returns no usable calls with usage metered; a socket idle/deadline cut rejects with a retryable error.
primitives.example: const provider = new OllamaProvider({ model: 'llama3' });

primitives.name: OpenAIProvider
primitives.when: you want OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint as the Loop's provider — tool-calling, toolChoice, and a custom baseUrl
primitives.fails: throws on a missing apiKey; a malformed tool-call JSON returns no usable calls with usage still metered (BA-27); a socket idle/deadline/transport cut rejects with a retryable error.
primitives.example: const provider = new OpenAIProvider({ apiKey, model: 'gpt-5' });

primitives.name: Planner
primitives.when: you need to turn a goal into an ordered step DAG for an LLM to execute — optionally forcing exactly N independent steps for fan-out
primitives.fails: throws if constructed without a provider; a plan call's HaltError (governance cap) propagates clean. Plan-call usage forwards via onLlmResult.

primitives.name: readDeferQueue
primitives.when: you want to read the deferred-action queue and reconstruct each id's live status (an external waker or a status check)
primitives.fails: never throws on a missing/empty queue; folds append-only status lines (latest wins) and returns the reconstructed records.
primitives.example: const queue = await readDeferQueue();

primitives.name: recurse
primitives.when: a task is too big for one model pass and you want it split, fanned out, verified, and merged — with total cost capped by a gate
primitives.signature: recurse(task: string, ctx?: RecurseCtx, opts?: RecurseOptions) => Promise<RecurseResult>
primitives.fails: returns `{incomplete, best}` on guard exhaustion or a dead worker (never a faked pass); a gate HaltError exits clean. Cost is open by design — run under a budget gate.

primitives.name: refine
primitives.when: you have a caller-supplied attempt + evaluate pair and want to iterate generate → grade → regenerate until it passes or hits a bound
primitives.fails: returns the last outcome on maxIterations or a terminal `failed` verdict (never a faked pass); a HaltError from either callback propagates clean.
primitives.example:
const { result, passed } = await refine({ attempt, evaluate, maxIterations: 3 });
if (!passed) escalate(result);

primitives.name: remember
primitives.when: you want to distill durable facts from harvested transcript spans and persist them through a Store socket (the consolidation pass)
primitives.signature: remember(spans: Array<string | { content?: string, text?: string }>, options: RememberOptions) => Promise<RememberOutcome>
primitives.fails: skips empty spans and never fabricates; a provider HaltError propagates clean. Each pass forwards usage via onLlmResult; a fact counts once via ctx.recordMemoryOp.
primitives.example:
const { facts } = await remember(spans, { provider, store });
console.log(`consolidated ${facts.length} durable facts`);

primitives.name: Retry
primitives.when: you want backoff-with-jitter around a flaky async call (a provider request, a plan step) — the retry seam Loop and runPlan wrap providers with
primitives.fails: rethrows the last error once attempts are exhausted; by default only transient errors (429/5xx/ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT) are retried.
primitives.example:
const retry = new Retry({ maxAttempts: 3, jitter: true });
const res = await retry.call(() => provider.generate(msgs));

primitives.name: runPlan
primitives.when: you have a step DAG from the Planner and want to execute it with wave-based parallelism (independent steps run concurrently)
primitives.signature: runPlan(steps: Step[], executeFn: (step: Step) => any, options?: RunPlanOptions) => Promise<StepResult[]>
primitives.fails: throws on a malformed DAG (empty steps, non-function executeFn, duplicate ids, unknown dependency); a step's own error surfaces per StepResult, never crashing the wave.
primitives.example:
const steps = await planner.plan(goal);
const results = await runPlan(steps, step => execute(step));

primitives.name: Scheduler
primitives.when: you need to fire agent turns on a schedule — cron expressions or relative intervals — driven by a periodic tick
primitives.fails: an errored job routes to the onError handler and never crashes the tick loop; a malformed cron/interval is rejected when the job is added.
primitives.example:
const sched = new Scheduler({ interval: 60000 });
sched.add({ id: 'poll', cron: '0 * * * *', run });

primitives.name: SkillRegistry
primitives.when: you want to expose operator-registered skill bundles to a model by progressive disclosure — one meta-tool whose catalog unlocks a skill's tools on demand
primitives.fails: register() rejects an unsafe or colliding name fail-fast and commits nothing on failure; governance is unchanged — discovery never authorizes.

primitives.name: spawnChild
primitives.when: you want to fork a child bareagent process programmatically and get a handle — heavyweight delegation, not the in-process recurse default
primitives.fails: bounded by timeoutMs (wall-clock) and opt-in idleTimeoutMs (heartbeat); the result carries idleKilled if the watchdog fired. Threads BAREGUARD env vars to the child.
primitives.example:
const handle = spawnChild({ config, input });
const result = await handle.wait();

primitives.name: SQLite
primitives.when: you want durable, queryable SQLite-backed storage for Memory (store/search/get/delete) persisted on disk
primitives.fails: throws on a missing path or an absent better-sqlite3 peer dep; implements the four-verb Store socket.
primitives.example: const store = new SQLite({ path: './agent.db' });

primitives.name: StateMachine
primitives.when: you need to track task lifecycle (pending/running/done/failed/waiting/cancelled) with enforced transitions and optional file persistence
primitives.fails: rejects an illegal state transition and never throws on a valid one; state changes are emitted as events.
primitives.example:
const sm = new StateMachine();
sm.create('t1'); sm.transition('t1', 'running');

primitives.name: Stream
primitives.when: you want a structured event emitter for loop/tool/governance events, optionally piped to a transport sink
primitives.fails: never throws on emit; a transport write error is isolated and does not interrupt the run.
primitives.example:
const stream = new Stream({ transport });
stream.emit('loop:round', { n: 1 });

primitives.name: unitAssembler
primitives.when: you want to adapt a litectx-style neutral-unit assemble(units, ctx) verb into the Loop's assemble(msgs, ctx) context-assembly seam
primitives.signature: unitAssembler(assembleUnits: (units: Array<Record<string, any>>, ctx: any) => (any | Promise<any>)) => (msgs: Array<Record<string, any>>, ctx: any) => Promise<Array<Record<string, any>>>
primitives.fails: fail-open — any unexpected return shape sends the original msgs unchanged; a thrown error (incl. HaltError) is left to the Loop's own handling.
primitives.example: const loop = new Loop({ provider, assemble: unitAssembler(litectx.assemble) });

primitives.name: unitTrimmer
primitives.when: you want to adapt litectx's trim(units, policy) verb into the Loop's destructive trim(msgs, ctx) seam — harvest-before-evict with an F2 residual .flush
primitives.signature: unitTrimmer(opts?: { trim?: Function, onHarvest?: Function, policy?: any }) => ((msgs: Array<Record<string, any>>, ctx?: any) => Promise<Array<Record<string, any>>>) & { flush: (msgs: Array<Record<string, any>>, ctx?: any) => Promise<void> }
primitives.fails: throws if the trim/onHarvest verbs are missing (runtime-checked); the fold is fail-open and a HaltError propagates. `.flush` drains the residual harvest.
primitives.example: const loop = new Loop({ provider, trim: unitTrimmer({ trim: litectx.trim, onHarvest, policy: { keepLastN: 20 } }) });

primitives.name: wireGate
primitives.when: you have a bareguard Gate and want to wire it into a Loop as the policy + metering chokepoint in one line
primitives.signature: wireGate(gate: Gate, options?: object) => {policy: Function, onLlmResult: Function, onToolResult: Function, filterTools: Function, wrapTool: Function, wrapTools: Function}
primitives.fails: never throws; a gate halt surfaces as a HaltError the Loop catches and exits cleanly, and a deny is an advisory string fed back to the model.
